findings.reason: The protected Python solution evaluates minimum leaf flips via postorder tree DP using an explicit visited-state stack to avoid recursion stack overflow. For each node, it computes costs = (min_flips_for_false, min_flips_for_true). Leaves cost (0, 1) or (1, 0), NOT nodes swap child costs, and binary operators (OR, AND, XOR) evaluate all 4 child outcome combinations. The solution runs in O(n) time and O(n) space; no candidate is required.

Postorder evaluation guarantees child minimum flip pairs are computed before parent evaluation. Evaluating all 4 combinations of left/right Boolean states per binary node and picking min cost for each outcome (False / True) strictly minimizes total leaf flips.
Each tree node is visited twice (push/pop) and evaluated in constant time, yielding O(n) time and O(n) space for stack and DP costs dictionary. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts root TreeNode and target boolean result, returning minimum leaf flips costs[root][result].

The approach accurately details postorder tree DP pair tracking, operator cost combination logic, explicit stack recursion-safety, and O(n) time / O(n) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover recursive tree DP overflow risks, greedy evaluation pitfalls, single-leaf roots, unary NOT child orientation, and XOR semantics.
